authority_basis.claim_scope: Newtonian inverse-square attractive interaction for point masses.
External gravitational force of a spherically symmetric source may be treated as if its mass were concentrated at its centre.
Mutual gravitational forces form an equal-and-opposite interaction pair on distinct bodies.

concepts.statement: In the Newtonian model, two masses exert mutual attractive forces along the line joining their centres or point-mass locations.
concepts.why_required: The force direction is fixed by source-receiver geometry rather than by motion direction or drawing orientation.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Learners may make gravity follow velocity, page-down direction, or only falling motion.

concepts.statement: Outside a spherically symmetric mass distribution, the Newtonian gravitational interaction is equivalent to using the total source mass at the centre.
concepts.why_required: The inverse-square point-source relation needs an explicit model bridge when applied to planets or spherical bodies.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: The point-mass equation may be applied to extended bodies without stating when the reduction is legitimate.

conditions: Point masses or valid external spherical-symmetry reduction

symbols.name: force on receiver due to source
outward unit vector from source to receiver

model_conditions.condition: The Newtonian weak-field, non-relativistic gravitational model is adequate for the requested scale.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The inverse-square Newtonian force law is the intended Grade 9-11 engineering model for ordinary planetary and laboratory contexts.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Strong-field or relativistic regimes require a different gravitational model.

model_conditions.condition: Each source is a point mass or the receiver is outside a spherically symmetric source so the external spherical reduction is valid.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The simple centre-to-centre inverse-square relation otherwise does not encode the full extended mass distribution.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: The mass distribution must be integrated or otherwise modelled explicitly.

representations.semantic_geometry: Two masses are joined by their centre-to-centre line, with equal-and-opposite attractive force vectors on distinct receivers and an explicit separation r.
must_not_imply: gravity acts only when an object is falling
the two third-law forces act on the same body
representations.verification_method: Check both force vectors lie on the source-receiver line, point toward the other mass, and form an equal-and-opposite third-law pair.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify the two interacting masses and name the receiver for the force being computed.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A magnitude can be computed without a physically defined force-on-body quantity.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Check the Newtonian point-mass or external spherical-symmetry model and define the separation r.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The inverse-square equation may be applied outside its stated geometric/model scope.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Compute the inverse-square magnitude and assign the attractive direction toward the other mass.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Magnitude and direction may be mixed or the vector sign may be assigned from motion rather than geometry.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Verify units, third-law pairing, model validity and inverse-square limiting behaviour as separation changes.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A distance, body-label or direction error can survive the forward calculation.

required_transformations.description: Translate a gravity narrative into an explicit source-receiver interaction before inserting values into the inverse-square relation.
Bind the computed magnitude to the source-receiver geometry so the force vector points toward the attracting source.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Gravity acts only while an object is falling downward and disappears while the object is supported or moving upward.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Everyday language often associates gravity with falling events rather than with a persistent mass-mass interaction.
trigger_contexts: parachutist before and after opening parachute
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A supported book still has a measurable weight force while the support supplies an opposing contact force.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Show the gravitational interaction arrow on the object in supported, rising and falling states.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Treat gravity as an interaction present whenever the masses and Newtonian model apply; motion state does not switch it on or off.
misconceptions.verification: Compare FBDs for supported, rising and falling states and confirm the gravity interaction remains present.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: The gravitational-force direction follows the object's velocity or trajectory direction.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Motion arrows and force arrows are often visually conflated in trajectory diagrams.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: An upward-moving projectile near Earth still has downward gravitational force toward Earth.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Place velocity and gravitational-force vectors side by side with separate labels and different geometric roles.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Determine force direction from source-receiver geometry, independent of instantaneous velocity.
misconceptions.verification: Reverse the velocity direction without changing source position; the gravitational-force direction must remain toward the source.

problem_families.name: Two-mass Newtonian gravitational force
problem_families.first_technical_move: Name the receiver and define centre-to-centre separation before using the inverse-square law.
fatal_errors: placing both third-law forces on one body

problem_families.name: External force of a spherical source
problem_families.first_technical_move: Check that the receiver is outside the spherically symmetric source and measure r from the source centre.
fatal_errors: measuring r from the surface when the equation requires centre distance
using the external reduction inside the source
